title: Sukuh
visualBrief: Specific standing Sukuh core: broad flat-topped sloping stone pyramid with true narrow west stair channel and dressed cheeks/upper lintel, moulded summit band, low north/south platforms, small Bhimaswarga relief shrine, original simplified stela/Garuda/turtle vocabulary, western tapered stone gateway with real passage and Kala-like lintel relief, and short terrain-following terrace retaining edges/approaches. Preserve open native-ground courts and independent modern buildings. No roofed summit restoration, copied narrative/text relief or complete interiors.

sourceFacts.horizontalBasis: Exact-QID Q3101506/way646444755 and named standard building/POI35185018533587 establish the main approximately16.5x14.8m pyramid. Four additional map controls35185018533590..35185018533593 align with the western gate, north platform, south platform and small shrine in the ordinary precinct sketch. Anchor111.131537336,-7.627315249; heading0, internal local+x angle+.054081447315rad, west-front along local-x. Main mapped dimensions/positions are retained; internal stair, sculpture and terrace allocation are picture/map-led approximations.

reconstruction.terrainBasis: Retain original standard6m Mapzen ground/water and independent buildings. Small local level bases have constant buried bottoms sampled along all boundaries. Main pyramid front threshold follows local west grade; its lower body is buried into uphill grade. Gate and detached platforms use separate local floors; short approach steps and narrow retaining edges follow native slope. No broad flattened terrace/island slab or ground/water cutout. Coarse wooded DEM does not resolve exact archaeological terrace/paving/door thresholds; relative and absolute elevations remain approximate.
